Declared independent-unit column piling_id is consistent with the frozen data in both arms: each of the 12 pilings appears on exactly 4 rows (one per depth band), every piling carries a single coating_system across all its rows, and pilings split 6/6 between coal_tar_epoxy and glassflake_polyester.

The selected result demonstrates the issue: scipy.stats.ttest_ind, a row-independent two-sample t test, was run on all 48 rows even though each piling contributes 4 correlated depth-band readings; the report states '48 gauge readings from 12 pilings', 'one observation per gauge reading', reports t(46) (df = 48-2 instead of 12-2 = 10), and explicitly says 'All 48 rows were entered into the test as separate observations' — textbook pseudoreplication of the piling unit.

Within-piling readings are visibly non-independent (monotone decrease with depth within every piling), so treating rows as independent inflates the effective sample size and understates the p-value; no piling-level aggregation or clustered/mixed model was applied to the tested quantity.

The minted lock's authorized_key_columns is exactly ['piling_id'], matching the declaration's independent-unit column, so the unit-key authorization follows from the declaration alone; the lock's stated limitations correctly do not extend to endorsing the row-independent test itself.

The declared independent-unit column print_run_id is consistent with the frozen data: there are 8 runs (R01-R08) each contributing exactly 3 coupon rows, and laser_setting is constant within every run (R01-R04 all nominal, R05-R08 all elevated), matching the description that the treatment is applied once per run and all build conditions are shared within a run. Both procedure arms (nominal and elevated) are composed of whole runs, so the run is the unit to which treatment was assigned in both arms.

The selected report demonstrates the issue on its face: it applies a two-sided Fisher exact test to a 2x2 table in which 'each coupon row supplies one observation', yielding n=24 (12 vs 12), while simultaneously stating the 24 rows span only 8 print runs. Fisher's exact test assumes independent observations, but the three coupons from a run share the run's powder lot, recoater condition, gas flow, and thermal history and are explicitly not expected to be independent; the effective number of independent units per arm is 4 runs, not 12 coupons.

The pseudoreplication is material to the stated conclusion: the reported p = 0.0094 comes from treating 24 correlated coupon rows as independent trials. Aggregated at the run level the comparison is 4 nominal runs versus 4 elevated runs, which cannot achieve comparable significance under an exact test, so the row-level p-value overstates the evidence.
No authority lock was minted, so lock conformance is not applicable.

The report demonstrates absence of the issue: it states the 46 rows are repeated sessions, shows a tank-level table whose session counts (4,4,4,4,3,4,4,4,4,3,4,4) sum to 46, and runs the Mann-Whitney on 12 tank means (6 vs 6), never on session rows.

Recomputation confirms tank-level analysis: tank means match the raw data (e.g., T05 = 219.30 from 3 sessions, T10 = 233.10 from 3 sessions), U = 34 matches the ranking of the 12 tank means, exact two-sided p = 8/924 = 0.008658, and rank-biserial = 2*34/(6*6) - 1 = 0.889, all as reported; these values are only attainable with n = 6 per group, not with row-level n.

The minted lock authorizes key columns ["tank_id"], exactly the declared independent-unit column, scoped to this case, input digest, and the mannwhitneyu procedure, so the unit-key authorization follows from the declaration alone.
